rv.q: The Met’s “Tosca,” by contrast, was hot-blooded from beginning to end.
Marina Rebeka, singing her first-ever Tosca, displayed the power and temperament required for the role.
For those who like full-throated, unapologetically dramatic singing, this is a dream cast for you.
Sometimes it takes a new voice to make you hear old music as if for the first time.
On this evening, the soprano didn’t disappoint and proved to be fearless in her incarnation of Tosca, even if the rest of her company was not quite on her level.

cn.t: Hernández's fearless Met debut anchors a vocally thrilling but unevenly staged *Tosca*. Critics praise the dream cast's full-throated drama while noting the production feels dated.
